name: Talbot-Lago T26C
description:
T26C: 6 cyl in-line, 93 * 110mm = 4483cc, naturally aspirated, twin high camshafts, 260 bhp @ 5000 rpm

Design: Antonio Lago / Carlo Marchetti
Transmission: 4 speed Wilson pre-selector
Chassis: Steel box-section frame, aluminium body
Suspension: Front: wishbones, transverse leaf spring Rear: live axle, semi-elliptic leaf springs
Dimensions: Wheelbase: 2502mm, weight: 950 kg
Top speed: 270 km/h
Years: 1948-1951

The unblown half of the 1946 formula, and the half nobody took seriously until the fuel bills arrived. Where a two-stage Maserati drank a gallon every two miles, the big Talbot six could run a whole Grand Prix without stopping - which is how Louis Rosier won the 1949 Belgian Grand Prix over three and a half hours without once leaving the car, and how Louis Chiron took the French Grand Prix at Reims the same summer.

1948-49 specification: 260 bhp. The 1950 T26C-DA, with twin plugs and revised carburation, made 280.
